statements.text: The last bell went twenty minutes ago. The room still smells of chalk and hot dust.

statements.speaker: nao
statements.text: Everyone's gone home. I wanted to record the room before they lock the building.

options.text: Say nothing, and listen with her.

statements.text: So you say nothing. The cicadas fill the gap where the answer would have been.

statements.speaker: nao
statements.text: Thank you. Most people start talking the second I hold this up.

statements.speaker: you
statements.text: What is there to record? It's an empty room.

statements.speaker: nao
statements.text: It's not empty. It's just quiet. Those aren't the same, and I can prove it.
She holds the recorder out at arm's length. The fluorescent tubes tick overhead. Somewhere below, a door closes.

statements.speaker: nao
statements.text: There. That's the building settling. It does that every evening at about this time.

statements.speaker: nao
statements.text: You heard it too. I could tell. You went still.
She stops the recorder without looking at it, the way you stop a clock you already trust.

statements.speaker: nao
statements.text: You'll hear it on the playback. Probably. It's under everything else we said.
She winds the cable around the recorder twice, and does not offer to play it back.

stages.brief: An original empty classroom in late afternoon, warm light, rice fields through the open windows, no people
The same empty classroom at blue hour, ceiling lights on, the fields outside gone dark, no people

tracks.brief: Sparse piano over cicadas, unhurried, a little hollow
